title: site-astro has two independent stylesheets that must be hand-kept in sync
summary: site-astro has no shared global stylesheet or CSS custom-property source of truth: index.astro imports landing.css while docs.astro, blog/index.astro, and BlogPostLayout.astro all import docs.css instead — the two files define the same-named tokens (--display/--sans/--mono/--frost/--ember/etc) independently, so a redesign applied to one (as happened earlier this session, when landing.css was fully re-themed) leaves the other silently stale until someone notices the mismatch by eye.
incidentAliases: docs page looks different from home

title: site-astro has two independent stylesheets that must be hand-kept in sync
summary: site-astro has no shared global stylesheet or CSS custom-property source of truth: index.astro imports landing.css while docs.astro, blog/index.astro and BlogPostLayout.astro import docs.css instead — the two define the same-named tokens (--display/--sans/--mono/--frost/--ember/etc) independently, so a redesign applied to one leaves the other silently stale. A third stylesheet, how.css, was added for the how-it-works pages and deliberately does NOT follow that pattern: it defines no tokens of its own and is imported alongside docs.css, riding its tokens and chrome, with every rule scoped under body.how-page so it cannot leak into docs or blog which share that same docs.css. Prefer the how.css ride-on pattern for any new page family — it is the only one of the three that cannot drift.

title: site-astro has two independent stylesheets that must be hand-kept in sync
summary: site-astro has no shared global stylesheet or CSS custom-property source of truth: index.astro imports landing.css while docs.astro, blog/index.astro and BlogPostLayout.astro import docs.css instead — the two define the same-named tokens (--display/--sans/--mono/--frost/--ember/etc) independently, so a redesign applied to one leaves the other silently stale. A third stylesheet, how.css, was added for the how-it-works pages and deliberately does NOT follow that pattern: it defines no tokens of its own and is imported alongside docs.css, riding its tokens and chrome, with every rule scoped under body.how-page so it cannot leak into docs or blog which share that same docs.css. What makes the ride-on possible is that docs.css declares its palette on a bare :root with no body-class qualifier — so any page can pick its own body class and still inherit the full dark token set (body.essay-page re-scopes to a LIGHT palette; that is the one body class that changes the theme). Prefer the how.css ride-on pattern for any new page family — it is the only one of the three that cannot drift.

title: site-astro has two independent stylesheets that must be hand-kept in sync
summary: site-astro has no shared global stylesheet or CSS custom-property source of truth: index.astro imports landing.css while docs.astro, blog/index.astro and BlogPostLayout.astro import docs.css instead — the two define the same-named tokens (--display/--sans/--mono/--frost/--ember/etc) AND the same nav layout rules (height, gap, z-index, mobile-menu offsets) independently, so a change to one leaves the other silently stale. A third stylesheet, how.css, rides docs.css's tokens/chrome instead of duplicating them and is the pattern to prefer for new page families.
